claims.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: The inverse images of the six surviving vertices under any sequence of vertex deletions and edge contractions are pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected branch sets. Two quotient vertices are adjacent exactly when their branch sets have an edge between them, so the unique missing edge is precisely the A–B anticompleteness condition. Conversely, delete unused vertices and contract each connected set; the prescribed adjacencies give exactly K6 minus AB. A seven-label assignment is an O(n)-size certificate. Exhausting all 7^n assignments and checking connectivity and the 15 inter-label pair conditions by adjacency scans takes O(7^n n²).
claims.witness: A yes-certificate is the map V(G)→{unused,A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4} satisfying the stated nonemptiness, connectivity, and adjacency conditions.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the branch-set quotient equivalence directly from the permitted induced-minor operations and exact-check-tested all one-extra-vertex quotient possibilities for K_t minus an edge, t=3,…,6.

claims.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
claims.evidence: If q=0, every two nonempty disjoint sets are adjacent, so no exceptional anticomplete pair exists. If q>0 and there are four universal vertices, the endpoints of any nonedge together with those four vertices induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices. Every other vertex is an endpoint of at least one complement edge, and q complement edges have at most 2q distinct endpoints; hence n≤2q+3. Applying Claim 0's enumeration gives O(7^(2q+3)n²). If q=O(log n), the exponential factor is n^{O(1)}. The exact checker verified both immediate decisions and the residual-size inequality over every labeled seven-vertex graph.
claims.witness: For the immediate yes case, any nonedge uv and any four universal vertices form the required six-vertex induced subgraph; otherwise the retained graph itself is the at-most-(2q+3)-vertex kernel.
claims.search_method: Proved the complement-edge endpoint bound and exhaustively checked it, including both decided cases, over all 2^21 labeled seven-vertex graphs using integer bit masks.

claims.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
claims.evidence: For a K_t−e model with exceptional sets A,B and cores C1,…,C_{t−2}, each core supplies an A–B path internally contained in that core. Thus every A–B separator disjoint from A∪B has size at least t−2. Choose an inclusion-minimal such separator S. Minimality gives full A- and B-side components, and chordality makes S a clique: two nonadjacent separator vertices, joined by shortest paths through the two full components, would give an induced cycle. Each full component contains an S-complete vertex. Indeed, choose v maximizing |N(v)∩S|; if v misses s∈S, a shortest path to a neighbor of s and chordality force its final vertex to see N(v)∩S as well as s, contradicting maximality. S-complete vertices x and y from the two sides are nonadjacent, so x,y plus any t−2 vertices of S induce K_t−e. The converse is immediate. For t=6, enumerating six vertices costs O(n^6). Exact exhaustion found no mismatch for all chordal graphs on t+1 vertices for every t=3,…,6.
claims.witness: From any model, the proof constructs an induced copy on {x,y}∪S0, where S0 is any (t−2)-subset of the minimal separator S.
claims.search_method: Completed the minimal-separator proof and independently exhausted 2,131,008 labeled graphs across t=3,…,6; 636,712 were chordal and none had an induced-minor/induced-subgraph mismatch.

claims.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
claims.evidence: In a complete multipartite graph, anticompleteness forces both exceptional branch sets into one part; that part is independent, so connectivity forces both sets to be singletons. A core branch is either a singleton in another part or spans at least two parts. Any spanning core can be shrunk to one cross-part edge, which remains adjacent to both exceptional vertices and to every other core. Singleton cores must occupy distinct nonexceptional parts. Consequently, after reserving the exceptional pair and s singleton cores, the remaining 4−s cores exist exactly when the residual multipartite graph has a matching of that size. Any matching has size at most floor(M/2) and M−L; if L>M/2, match every outside vertex to the largest part, while if L≤M/2, repeated cross-part pairing attains floor(M/2). Thus the formula and criterion are exact and enumerable in polynomial time.
claims.witness: An accepting tuple (i,s,J), together with 4−s disjoint cross-part matching edges, directly supplies the two exceptional singleton sets and the four core branch sets.
claims.search_method: Compared the criterion against direct enumeration of all connected core branch sets for all 96 integer part vectors of total order at most nine, and independently compared the matching formula with exact subset-DP matchings for 138 part vectors of total order at most ten.

claims.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
claims.evidence: On an edge-introducing nice decomposition, a state records each bag vertex's one of seven labels, the connectivity partition of vertices bearing each nonzero label, one of unseen/active/completed for each of six labels, and 14 required-adjacency bits. An introduced same-label edge merges blocks; a different allowed-label edge sets its bit; an A–B edge rejects. When forgetting the last boundary vertex of one component, the separator property makes future reconnection impossible: the transition is valid only if no other component of that label remains, after which the label is completed. At joins, assignments agree, partitions take transitive closure, bits are unioned, and two completed off-bag copies of one label are rejected. The empty root accepts exactly when all six labels are completed and all 14 bits are set. There are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a pattern-dependent constant states, and even quadratic join processing remains 2^{O(w log w)}. A nice decomposition has O(nw) nodes/edge introductions, absorbed into n·2^{O(w log w)}. The persisted exact reference DP exercised every transition, including joins and a genuinely contracted two-vertex branch set.
claims.witness: An accepting root state has an empty bag, all six labels completed as single connected branch sets, no forbidden A–B edge, and all fourteen required adjacency bits set.
claims.search_method: Specified and checked the full state invariant and transitions; ran an exact tuple/integer-bit-mask implementation on a width-4 join decomposition, a one-required-edge-missing rejection, and a width-5 model requiring a two-vertex contracted branch.

claims.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
claims.evidence: The two four-vertex paths and the four singleton c_i sets form the displayed model. If an exceptional set were {x}, its four disjoint core neighbors would require at least four distinct neighbors of x. Every path vertex has degree at most three, so x=c_i. The other connected exceptional set Y must lie in one interval component of A−a_i or B−b_i because it is anticomplete to c_i. Exact enumeration of all 1,676 connected subsets and all choices of x,Y leaves only eight symmetric cases after requiring four available neighbors for each exception. In each, Y has exactly four external neighbors, including a path endpoint isolated in G−({x}∪Y). The four disjoint core sets must use the four boundary vertices separately; the isolated endpoint's core is therefore its singleton and has no edge to the other three cores, a contradiction. Hence no model has either exceptional branch singleton.
claims.witness: Vertices A={a1,a2,a3,a4}, B={b1,b2,b3,b4}, and singleton cores {c1},…,{c4}, with path edges, all six clique edges among the c_i, attachments a_i c_i and b_i c_i, and no other edges.
claims.search_method: Validated the displayed model and exhaustively enumerated every connected candidate for the nonsingleton exception using exact integer bit masks; the eight surviving boundary configurations were all rejected by the isolated-boundary-vertex argument.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for the unrestricted complexity classification of detecting K6 minus an edge as an induced minor and, if tractable, a polynomial-time algorithm. The draft explicitly says that the unrestricted P-versus-NP-complete classification remains unresolved. Its verified contributions—an exact exponential certificate algorithm, FPT in the number of nonedges, polynomial algorithms on chordal, complete-multipartite, and supplied bounded-treewidth inputs, and a normalization obstruction—are material but do not settle unrestricted tractability or hardness. Thus they constitute valid partial progress, and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source JSON and baseline draft JSON; used the exact target rather than the claim list to judge coverage.
Reconstructed every proof independently, including all quantifiers and both directions of each equivalence.
Compiled and ran audit_graph_exhaustive.cpp using exact integer bit masks over 2,131,008 labeled graphs; no chordal mismatch or dense-kernel rule failure was found.
Ran audit_structured_models.py: direct multipartite branch-set search matched the criterion on 96 part vectors, and exact matching DP matched the formula on 138 vectors.
The same structured checker enumerated all 1,676 connected subsets of the 12-vertex construction and reduced all singleton-exception candidates to eight explicitly rejected configurations.
Ran audit_treewidth_dp.py, an exact reference implementation of introduce-vertex, introduce-edge, forget, and join transitions; its positive, negative, and contracted-branch tests all passed.
No floating-point decision procedure was used.
